title: Research: restricted three-register AGL2 target triple costs six calls
body:
## Result

For the exact three-register formal model `M_3(F2[AGL_2(F2)])`, the target
`diag([a],[b],[h])`, with `h = a*b*a*t_x`, has minimum paid-call cost six when the paid address labels are restricted to `{a,b,t_x}`. The target acts as `h(x0,x1) = (x1,x0+1)` on its third register. Arbitrary free scalar `GL_3(F2)` mixing is included and normalized by augmentation; all three register inputs are arbitrary dirty data.

The direct six-call word is exact. A complete radius-three group-algebra BFS and all 4,782 radius-two/radius-three joins found no word through five calls. The formal layers contain 1, 84, 4,697, and 232,720 distinct states. The homogeneous displacement-rank relaxation is four calls, so this closes the two-call gap for this restricted alphabet. This is a scoped negative result; it does not change the selected conditional bound or `kappa`.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-affine-mixed-target-triple-seed818dbf
```

Expected markers:

```text
PASS_BIT_AFFINE_MIXED_TARGET_TRIPLE group=24 generators=84 layers=1,84,4697,232720 probes=4782 minimum=6 hit=False
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-affine-mixed-target-triple-seed818dbf outcome=negative-result
```

The package includes the formal word model, exact layer digests, an independent dense multiplication control, all 84 generator inverse checks, direct-word omissions, wrong-label and wrong-target controls, source pins, and the stopping rule.

## Assignment and overlap

Seed `818dbf90f2581f79a4e4150cdd77e415`, track `bit-mechanisms`, task `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 3. Exact base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

PR #1696 treats the related linear `GL_2(F2)` target `(a,b,aba)` on three registers. PR #1711 treats two affine targets on two registers with the four-label alphabet `{a,b,t_x,t_y}`. This result uses the mixed three-target endpoint `(a,b,h)` on three registers and only `{a,b,t_x}`. The refreshed repository-scoped AGL2 Discussion search found only #1317, where this claim is tracked: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18918291 .

PR #1333 supplies the broader affine displacement-rank theorem; its argument is credited and not claimed as new. Prepared by Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in experiment design, exact-search implementation, and package drafting.
